_meta.indication: DAYBUE is indicated for the treatment of Rett syndrome in adults and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older.

pivotal_trials.population: Female patients aged 5 to 20 years with typical Rett syndrome and a documented disease-causing mutation in the MECP2 gene
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary: change from baseline at Week 12 in RSBQ total score and CGI-I score
pivotal_trials.result: RSBQ: LS mean treatment difference -3.2 (95% CI -5.7, -0.6), p=0.018; CGI-I: LS mean treatment difference -0.3 (95% CI -0.5, -0.1), p=0.003, both favoring DAYBUE

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and ≥2% greater than placebo) were diarrhea (82% vs 20% placebo) and vomiting (29% vs 12%). In Study 1 and in long-term studies, 85% of DAYBUE-treated patients experienced diarrhea, and diarrhea was the most common adverse reaction leading to discontinuation (15%).
target_moa: Trofinetide is a synthetic analog of the tripeptide glycine-proline-glutamate (GPE), a product of cleavage of IGF-1; the mechanism by which it exerts therapeutic effects in Rett syndrome is unknown.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee.

summary.text: Trofinetide (NDA 217026), a new molecular entity, received Priority review and was granted Fast Track (2013), Orphan Drug (2015), and Rare Pediatric Disease (2020) designations for Rett syndrome; Breakthrough Therapy designation was denied (2015). It was approved on a standard (non-accelerated) basis on the strength of one adequate and well-controlled trial (Study 003/ACP-2566-003) plus confirmatory evidence from Study 002.

citations.quote: Trofinetide is a new molecular entity (NME) that has not been approved for any indication and has not been the subject of a prior marketing application.

Trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome was granted Fast Track designation on June 4, 2013, Orphan Drug Designation on February 11, 2015, and Rare Pediatric Disease Designation on March 02, 2020, all predicated on the fact that Rett syndrome is a serious, rare condition with an unmet medical need.
The application meets the substantial evidence standard based on one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation plus confirmatory evidence.

The application for trofinetide includes data from one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation (Study 003) plus confirmatory evidence (Study 002). Study 003 was an adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation that showed a statistically significant difference between treatment and placebo on the co-primary endpoint, CFB on the RSBQ.
